   367→// Batch fetch session data (metadata.json and prompt.txt) using GraphQL
   368→// Returns a map of checkpointId -> { prompt, metadata } along with any failures
   369→export interface SessionData {
   370→  prompt: string | null;
   371→  agent: string;
   372→  steps: number;
   373→  sessionCount: number;
   374→  strategy: string | null;
   375→  createdAt: string;
   376→  branch: string | null; // Branch where checkpoint was created (from metadata.json)
   377→  // Additional metadata fields
   378→  sessionId: string | null;
   379→  filesTouched: string[] | null;
   380→  sessionIds: string[] | null;
   381→  transcriptUuidAtStart: string | null;
   382→  transcriptLinesAtStart: number | null;
   383→  // Token usage metrics
   384→  inputTokens: number | null;
   385→  cacheCreationTokens: number | null;
   386→  cacheReadTokens: number | null;
   387→  outputTokens: number | null;
   388→  apiCallCount: number | null;
   389→}
   390→
   391→export async function fetchSessionDataBatch(
   392→  repoFullName: string,
   393→  checkpointIds: string[],
   394→  token: string
   395→): Promise<BatchResult<SessionData>> {
   396→  const results: BatchResult<SessionData> = {
   397→    data: new Map(),
   398→    failedItems: [],
   399→    errors: [],
   400→  };
   401→
   402→  // Filter to valid checkpoint IDs to prevent GraphQL injection
   403→  const invalidIds: string[] = [];
   404→  const validCheckpointIds = checkpointIds.filter((id) => {
   405→    if (!isValidCheckpointId(id)) {
   406→      console.warn(`[github-graphql] Skipping invalid checkpoint ID: ${id.slice(0, 10)}...`);
   407→      invalidIds.push(id);
   408→      return false;
   409→    }
   410→    return true;
   411→  });
   412→
   413→  // Track invalid IDs as failed items
   414→  results.failedItems.push(...invalidIds);
   415→
   416→  if (validCheckpointIds.length === 0) return results;
   417→
   418→  const [owner, repo] = repoFullName.split("/");
   419→
   420→  // Chunk into batches of 20 (40 blobs per batch - metadata + prompt)
   421→  const BATCH_SIZE = 20;
   422→  for (let i = 0; i < validCheckpointIds.length; i += BATCH_SIZE) {
   423→    const batch = validCheckpointIds.slice(i, i + BATCH_SIZE);
   424→
   425→    // Build dynamic query with aliases for each checkpoint's files
   426→    const fileQueries = batch
   427→      .map((checkpointId, idx) => {
   428→        const folderPath = `${checkpointId.slice(0, 2)}/${checkpointId.slice(2)}`;
   429→        return `
   430→          m${idx}: object(expression: "entire/sessions:${folderPath}/metadata.json") { ... on Blob { text } }
   431→          p${idx}: object(expression: "entire/sessions:${folderPath}/prompt.txt") { ... on Blob { text } }
   432→        `;
   433→      })
   434→      .join("\n");
   435→
   436→    const query = `
   437→      query SessionData($owner: String!, $repo: String!) {
   438→        repository(owner: $owner, name: $repo) {
   439→          ${fileQueries}
   440→        }
   441→      }
   442→    `;
   443→
   444→    try {
   445→      // Use partial data handling to extract successful results even if some fail
   446→      const result = await githubGraphQLPartial<{
   447→        repository: Record<string, { text: string } | null>;
   448→      }>(token, query, { owner, repo });
   449→
   450→      if (result.hasPartialData) {
   451→        console.warn(`[github-graphql] Partial success in session data batch:`, result.errors.map(e => e.message).join(", "));
   452→      }
   453→
   454→      if (result.data?.repository) {
   455→        batch.forEach((checkpointId, idx) => {
   456→          const metadata = result.data!.repository[`m${idx}`];
   457→          const prompt = result.data!.repository[`p${idx}`];
   458→
   459→          // If both metadata and prompt are null, this checkpoint may not exist
   460→          // Still record it with defaults so we don't repeatedly try to fetch it
   461→          let sessionData: SessionData = {
   462→            prompt: prompt?.text?.split("\n")[0] ?? null,
   463→            agent: "Claude Code",
   464→            steps: 1,
   465→            sessionCount: 1,
   466→            strategy: null,
   467→            createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
   468→            branch: null,
   469→            sessionId: null,
   470→            filesTouched: null,
   471→            sessionIds: null,
   472→            transcriptUuidAtStart: null,
   473→            transcriptLinesAtStart: null,
   474→            inputTokens: null,
   475→            cacheCreationTokens: null,
   476→            cacheReadTokens: null,
   477→            outputTokens: null,
   478→            apiCallCount: null,
   479→          };
   480→
   481→          if (metadata?.text) {
   482→            try {
   483→              const parsed = JSON.parse(metadata.text);
   484→              const tokenUsage = parsed.token_usage ?? {};
   485→              sessionData = {
   486→                ...sessionData,
   487→                agent: parsed.agent ?? "Claude Code",
   488→                steps: parsed.steps_count ?? parsed.checkpoints_count ?? 1,
   489→                sessionCount: parsed.session_count ?? 1,
   490→                strategy: parsed.strategy ?? null,
   491→                createdAt: parsed.created_at ?? new Date().toISOString(),
   492→                branch: parsed.branch ?? null,
   493→                sessionId: parsed.session_id ?? null,
   494→                filesTouched: Array.isArray(parsed.files_touched) ? parsed.files_touched : null,
   495→                sessionIds: Array.isArray(parsed.session_ids) ? parsed.session_ids : null,
   496→                transcriptUuidAtStart: parsed.transcript_uuid_at_start ?? null,
   497→                transcriptLinesAtStart: typeof parsed.transcript_lines_at_start === "number" ? parsed.transcript_lines_at_start : null,
   498→                inputTokens: typeof tokenUsage.input_tokens === "number" ? tokenUsage.input_tokens : null,
   499→                cacheCreationTokens: typeof tokenUsage.cache_creation_tokens === "number" ? tokenUsage.cache_creation_tokens : null,
   500→                cacheReadTokens: typeof tokenUsage.cache_read_tokens === "number" ? tokenUsage.cache_read_tokens : null,
   501→                outputTokens: typeof tokenUsage.output_tokens === "number" ? tokenUsage.output_tokens : null,
   502→                apiCallCount: typeof tokenUsage.api_call_count === "number" ? tokenUsage.api_call_count : null,
   503→              };
   504→            } catch {
   505→              // Invalid JSON, use defaults
   506→            }
   507→          }
   508→
   509→          results.data.set(checkpointId, sessionData);
   510→        });
   511→      } else if (result.errors.length > 0) {
   512→        // No data at all - whole batch failed
   513→        const errorMsg = result.errors.map(e => e.message).join(", ");
   514→        console.error(`[github-graphql] Failed to fetch session data batch:`, errorMsg);
   515→        results.failedItems.push(...batch);
   516→        results.errors.push(`Batch ${i / BATCH_SIZE + 1}: ${errorMsg}`);
   517→      }
   518→    } catch (err) {
   519→      const errorMsg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
   520→      console.error(`[github-graphql] Failed to fetch session data batch:`, errorMsg);
   521→      results.failedItems.push(...batch);
   522→      results.errors.push(`Batch ${i / BATCH_SIZE + 1}: ${errorMsg}`);
   523→    }
   524→  }
   525→
   526→  return results;
   527→}

   581→// Fetch user's repositories with all data (for syncing to DB)
   582→// Paginates through all pages (max 10 pages = 1000 repos to avoid runaway requests)
   583→export async function fetchUserReposWithForks(
   584→  username: string,
   585→  accessToken?: string,
   586→): Promise<GitHubRepoRaw[]> {
   587→  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
   588→    Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
   589→    "User-Agent": "gh-social-api",
   590→    "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
   591→  };

   594→    headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${accessToken}`;
   595→  }
   596→
   597→  const allRepos: GitHubRepoRaw[] = [];
   598→  let page = 1;
   599→  const perPage = 100;
   600→  const maxPages = 10; // Cap at 1000 repos
   601→
   602→  while (page <= maxPages) {
   603→    const url = accessToken
   604→      ? `${GITHUB_API}/user/repos?sort=updated&per_page=${perPage}&page=${page}&affiliation=owner,collaborator,organization_member`
   605→      : `${GITHUB_API}/users/${username}/repos?sort=updated&per_page=${perPage}&page=${page}`;
   606→
   607→    const response = await fetch(url, { headers });
   608→
   609→    if (!response.ok) {
   610→      // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
   611→      response.body?.cancel();

   614→
   615→    const repos = await response.json<GitHubRepoRaw[]>();
   616→    allRepos.push(...repos);
   617→
   618→    if (repos.length < perPage) {
   619→      break;
   620→    }
   621→    page++;
   622→  }
   623→
   624→  return allRepos;
   625→}

   627→// Check if a branch exists in a repository
   628→// Returns: true (exists), false (doesn't exist), null (error/unknown)
   629→export async function checkBranchExists(
   630→  repoFullName: string,
   631→  branchName: string,
   632→  accessToken: string,
   633→): Promise<boolean | null> {
   634→  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
   635→    Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
   636→    "User-Agent": "entire-api",
   637→    "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
   638→    Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
   639→  };
   640→
   641→  const url = `${GITHUB_API}/repos/${repoFullName}/branches/${encodeURIComponent(branchName)}`;
   642→  const response = await fetch(url, { headers });
   643→
   644→  if (response.ok) {
   645→    // GitHub may redirect branch names (e.g., master -> main for default branch)
   646→    // Verify the returned branch name actually matches what we requested
   647→    const data = await response.json() as { name?: string };
   648→    if (data.name !== branchName) {
   649→      console.log(`[checkBranchExists] ${repoFullName}/${branchName} -> redirected to ${data.name}, treating as not found`);
   650→      return false;
   651→    }
   652→    return true;
   653→  }
   654→
   655→  // Cancel body for non-OK responses
   656→  response.body?.cancel();
   657→
   658→  // 404 = branch doesn't exist (definitive answer)
   659→  if (response.status === 404) {
   660→    return false;
   661→  }
   662→
   663→  // 403/429/5xx = unknown (rate limit, auth issue, server error)
   664→  console.error(`checkBranchExists error for ${repoFullName}/${branchName}: ${response.status}`);
   665→  return null;
   666→}

   718→// Check if any of the user's installations has access to a specific repo

   720→export async function checkRepoHasAppAccess(
   721→  repoFullName: string,

   727→  if (result.error && result.installations.length === 0) {

   732→  if (result.installations.length === 0) {

   734→    return false;
   735→  }
   736→
   737→  // Check each installation to see if it has access to the repo

   739→    const hasAccess = await checkInstallationHasRepo(
   740→      installation.id,
   741→      repoFullName,
   742→      accessToken
   743→    );
   744→    if (hasAccess === true) {
   745→      return true;
   746→    }
   747→    // Continue checking other installations even if one fails
   748→  }
   749→
   750→  // If we had errors during fetch, we can't be sure the answer is "no"
   751→  if (result.error) {

   755→  return false;

   758→// Check if a specific installation has access to a repo
   759→// Returns: true (found), false (not found), null (error)
   760→async function checkInstallationHasRepo(
   761→  installationId: number,
   762→  repoFullName: string,
   763→  accessToken: string,
   764→): Promise<boolean | null> {
   765→  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
   766→    Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
   767→    "User-Agent": "entire-api",
   768→    "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
   769→    Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
   770→  };
   771→
   772→  let page = 1;
   773→  const perPage = 100;
   774→  const maxPages = 10; // Cap at 1000 repos per installation
   775→
   776→  while (page <= maxPages) {
   777→    const url = `${GITHUB_API}/user/installations/${installationId}/repositories?per_page=${perPage}&page=${page}`;
   778→    const response = await fetch(url, { headers });
   779→
   780→    if (!response.ok) {
   781→      // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
   782→      response.body?.cancel();
   783→      console.error(`checkInstallationHasRepo error for installation ${installationId}: ${response.status}`);
   784→      return null;
   785→    }
   786→
   787→    const data = await response.json<{
   788→      total_count: number;
   789→      repositories: Array<{ full_name: string }>;
   790→    }>();
   791→
   792→    if (data.repositories.some((r) => r.full_name === repoFullName)) {
   793→      return true;
   794→    }
   795→
   796→    if (data.repositories.length < perPage) {
   797→      break;
   798→    }
   799→    page++;
   800→  }
   801→
   802→  return false;
   803→}

   805→// Cached version of checkRepoHasAppAccess - caches result in KV for 10 minutes
   806→// Note: Cache is per-user since different users have different access to repos
   807→export async function checkRepoHasAppAccessCached(
   808→  repoFullName: string,
   809→  userId: string,
   810→  accessToken: string,
   811→  cache: KVNamespace,
   812→): Promise<boolean | null> {
   813→  const cacheKey = `app_access:${userId}:${repoFullName}`;
   814→
   815→  // Try cache first
   816→  const cached = await cache.get(cacheKey);
   817→  if (cached !== null) {
   818→    if (cached === "true") return true;
   819→    if (cached === "false") return false;
   820→    return null; // "null" string
   821→  }
   822→
   823→  // Fetch fresh
   824→  const result = await checkRepoHasAppAccess(repoFullName, accessToken);
   825→
   826→  // Cache the result (10 min TTL - shorter since we can't easily invalidate per-user from webhooks)
   827→  const cacheValue = result === null ? "null" : String(result);
   828→  await cache.put(cacheKey, cacheValue, { expirationTtl: 60 * 10 });
   829→
   830→  return result;
   831→}

  1150→// Fetch commit activity for a single repository
  1151→// Returns weekly commit totals for the last 52 weeks with week_start timestamp
  1152→async function fetchSingleRepoCommitActivity(
  1153→  repoFullName: string,
  1154→  accessToken?: string,
  1155→  retries = 3,
  1156→): Promise<CommitActivityResult | null> {
  1157→  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
  1158→    Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
  1159→    "User-Agent": "entire-api",
  1160→    "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
  1161→  };
  1162→
  1163→  if (accessToken) {
  1164→    headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${accessToken}`;
  1165→  }
  1166→
  1167→  const response = await fetch(
  1168→    `${GITHUB_API}/repos/${repoFullName}/stats/commit_activity`,
  1169→    { headers },
  1170→  );
  1171→
  1172→  // GitHub returns 202 if stats are being computed - retry after delay
  1173→  if (response.status === 202) {
  1174→    // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
  1175→    response.body?.cancel();
  1176→    if (retries > 0) {
  1177→      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 2000));
  1178→      return fetchSingleRepoCommitActivity(
  1179→        repoFullName,
  1180→        accessToken,
  1181→        retries - 1,
  1182→      );
  1183→    }
  1184→    // Stats still computing after retries, return null
  1185→    return null;
  1186→  }
  1187→
  1188→  // 204 No Content means no data available
  1189→  if (response.status === 204) {
  1190→    // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
  1191→    response.body?.cancel();
  1192→    return null;
  1193→  }
  1194→
  1195→  if (!response.ok) {
  1196→    // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
  1197→    response.body?.cancel();
  1198→    // Return null for repos we can't access (404, 403, etc.)
  1199→    return null;
  1200→  }
  1201→
  1202→  // Check if response has content before parsing
  1203→  const text = await response.text();
  1204→  if (!text || text.trim() === "") {
  1205→    return null;
  1206→  }
  1207→
  1208→  let data: Array<{ days: number[]; total: number; week: number }>;
  1209→  try {
  1210→    data = JSON.parse(text);
  1211→  } catch {
  1212→    // Invalid JSON response
  1213→    return null;
  1214→  }
  1215→
  1216→  // GitHub returns empty array for repos with no commits
  1217→  if (!Array.isArray(data) || data.length === 0) {
  1218→    return null;
  1219→  }
  1220→
  1221→  // Return array of weekly totals (52 weeks) with week_start timestamp
  1222→  // The first element's 'week' field is the Unix timestamp of week 0
  1223→  return {
  1224→    weeks: data.map((week) => week.total),
  1225→    week_start: data[0].week,
  1226→  };
  1227→}

function isRateLimited(response: Response): { limited: boolean; resetAt?: number } {
  if (response.status === 429) {

    const fileQueries = batch
      .map((checkpointId, idx) => {
        const folderPath = `${checkpointId.slice(0, 2)}/${checkpointId.slice(2)}`;
        return `
          m${idx}: object(expression: "entire/sessions:${folderPath}/metadata.json") { ... on Blob { text } }
          p${idx}: object(expression: "entire/sessions:${folderPath}/prompt.txt") { ... on Blob { text } }
        `;
      })
      .join("\n");

    const query = `
      query SessionData($owner: String!, $repo: String!) {
        repository(owner: $owner, name: $repo) {
          ${fileQueries}
        }
      }
    `;

    try {
      // Use partial data handling to extract successful results even if some fail
      const result = await githubGraphQLPartial<{
        repository: Record<string, { text: string } | null>;
      }>(token, query, { owner, repo });

      if (result.hasPartialData) {
        console.warn(`[github-graphql] Partial success in session data batch:`, result.errors.map(e => e.message).join(", "));
      }

      if (result.data?.repository) {
        batch.forEach((checkpointId, idx) => {
          const metadata = result.data!.repository[`m${idx}`];
          const prompt = result.data!.repository[`p${idx}`];

          // If both metadata and prompt are null, this checkpoint may not exist
          // Still record it with defaults so we don't repeatedly try to fetch it
          let sessionData: SessionData = {
            prompt: prompt?.text?.split("\n")[0] ?? null,
            agent: "Claude Code",
            steps: 1,
            sessionCount: 1,
            strategy: null,
            createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
            branch: null,
            sessionId: null,
            filesTouched: null,
            sessionIds: null,
            transcriptUuidAtStart: null,
            transcriptLinesAtStart: null,
            inputTokens: null,
            cacheCreationTokens: null,
            cacheReadTokens: null,
            outputTokens: null,
            apiCallCount: null,
          };

          if (metadata?.text) {
            try {
              const parsed = JSON.parse(metadata.text);
              const tokenUsage = parsed.token_usage ?? {};
              sessionData = {
                ...sessionData,
                agent: parsed.agent ?? "Claude Code",
                steps: parsed.steps_count ?? parsed.checkpoints_count ?? 1,
                sessionCount: parsed.session_count ?? 1,
                strategy: parsed.strategy ?? null,
                createdAt: parsed.created_at ?? new Date().toISOString(),
                branch: parsed.branch ?? null,
                sessionId: parsed.session_id ?? null,
                filesTouched: Array.isArray(parsed.files_touched) ? parsed.files_touched : null,
                sessionIds: Array.isArray(parsed.session_ids) ? parsed.session_ids : null,
                transcriptUuidAtStart: parsed.transcript_uuid_at_start ?? null,
                transcriptLinesAtStart: typeof parsed.transcript_lines_at_start === "number" ? parsed.transcript_lines_at_start : null,
                inputTokens: typeof tokenUsage.input_tokens === "number" ? tokenUsage.input_tokens : null,
                cacheCreationTokens: typeof tokenUsage.cache_creation_tokens === "number" ? tokenUsage.cache_creation_tokens : null,
                cacheReadTokens: typeof tokenUsage.cache_read_tokens === "number" ? tokenUsage.cache_read_tokens : null,
                outputTokens: typeof tokenUsage.output_tokens === "number" ? tokenUsage.output_tokens : null,
                apiCallCount: typeof tokenUsage.api_call_count === "number" ? tokenUsage.api_call_count : null,
              };
            } catch {
              // Invalid JSON, use defaults
            }
          }

          results.data.set(checkpointId, sessionData);
        });
      } else if (result.errors.length > 0) {
        // No data at all - whole batch failed
        const errorMsg = result.errors.map(e => e.message).join(", ");
        console.error(`[github-graphql] Failed to fetch session data batch:`, errorMsg);
        results.failedItems.push(...batch);
        results.errors.push(`Batch ${i / BATCH_SIZE + 1}: ${errorMsg}`);
      }
    } catch (err) {
      const errorMsg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
      console.error(`[github-graphql] Failed to fetch session data batch:`, errorMsg);
      results.failedItems.push(...batch);
      results.errors.push(`Batch ${i / BATCH_SIZE + 1}: ${errorMsg}`);
    }
  }

  return results;
}

// Raw GitHub repo response type
export interface GitHubRepoRaw {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  full_name: string;
  description: string | null;
  html_url: string;
  stargazers_count: number;
  language: string | null;
  fork: boolean;
  private: boolean;

    admin: boolean;

}

// Convert GitHub permissions to a single permission level
export function getPermissionLevel(permissions?: GitHubRepoRaw["permissions"]): "admin" | "maintain" | "write" | "triage" | "read" {
  if (!permissions) return "read";
  if (permissions.admin) return "admin";
  if (permissions.maintain) return "maintain";
  if (permissions.push) return "write";
  if (permissions.triage) return "triage";
  return "read";
}

// Fetch user's repositories with all data (for syncing to DB)
// Paginates through all pages (max 10 pages = 1000 repos to avoid runaway requests)
export async function fetchUserReposWithForks(
  username: string,
  accessToken?: string,
): Promise<GitHubRepoRaw[]> {
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
    "User-Agent": "gh-social-api",
    "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
  };

  if (accessToken) {
    headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${accessToken}`;
  }

  const allRepos: GitHubRepoRaw[] = [];
  let page = 1;
  const perPage = 100;
  const maxPages = 10; // Cap at 1000 repos

  while (page <= maxPages) {
    const url = accessToken
      ? `${GITHUB_API}/user/repos?sort=updated&per_page=${perPage}&page=${page}&affiliation=owner,collaborator,organization_member`
      : `${GITHUB_API}/users/${username}/repos?sort=updated&per_page=${perPage}&page=${page}`;

    const response = await fetch(url, { headers });

    if (!response.ok) {
      // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
      response.body?.cancel();
      throw new Error(`GitHub API error: ${response.status}`);
    }

    const repos = await response.json<GitHubRepoRaw[]>();
    allRepos.push(...repos);

    if (repos.length < perPage) {
      break;
    }
    page++;
  }

  return allRepos;
}

// Check if a branch exists in a repository
// Returns: true (exists), false (doesn't exist), null (error/unknown)
export async function checkBranchExists(
  repoFullName: string,
  branchName: string,
  accessToken: string,
): Promise<boolean | null> {
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
    "User-Agent": "entire-api",
    "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
    Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
  };

  const url = `${GITHUB_API}/repos/${repoFullName}/branches/${encodeURIComponent(branchName)}`;
  const response = await fetch(url, { headers });

  if (response.ok) {
    // GitHub may redirect branch names (e.g., master -> main for default branch)
    // Verify the returned branch name actually matches what we requested
    const data = await response.json() as { name?: string };
    if (data.name !== branchName) {
      console.log(`[checkBranchExists] ${repoFullName}/${branchName} -> redirected to ${data.name}, treating as not found`);
      return false;
    }
    return true;
  }

  // Cancel body for non-OK responses
  response.body?.cancel();

  // 404 = branch doesn't exist (definitive answer)
  if (response.status === 404) {
    return false;
  }

  // 403/429/5xx = unknown (rate limit, auth issue, server error)
  console.error(`checkBranchExists error for ${repoFullName}/${branchName}: ${response.status}`);
  return null;
}

// Result type for installation fetch - includes error state
export type InstallationsResult = {
  installations: Array<{ id: number; account: { login: string } }>;
  error: boolean; // true if we encountered an error (partial results)
};

// Fetch all GitHub App installations the user has access to
// Returns error: true if we couldn't complete the fetch (for accurate downstream handling)
export async function fetchUserInstallations(
  accessToken: string,
): Promise<InstallationsResult> {
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
    "User-Agent": "entire-api",
    "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
    Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
  };

  const allInstallations: Array<{ id: number; account: { login: string } }> = [];
  let page = 1;
  const perPage = 100;
  const maxPages = 5; // Cap at 500 installations

  while (page <= maxPages) {
    const url = `${GITHUB_API}/user/installations?per_page=${perPage}&page=${page}`;
    const response = await fetch(url, { headers });

    if (!response.ok) {
      // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
      response.body?.cancel();
      console.error(`Failed to fetch user installations: ${response.status}`);
      return { installations: allInstallations, error: true };
    }

    const data = await response.json<{
      total_count: number;
      installations: Array<{ id: number; account: { login: string } }>;
    }>();

    allInstallations.push(...data.installations);

    if (data.installations.length < perPage) {
      break;
    }
    page++;
  }

  return { installations: allInstallations, error: false };
}

// Check if any of the user's installations has access to a specific repo
// Returns: true (has access), false (no access), null (error/unknown)
export async function checkRepoHasAppAccess(
  repoFullName: string,
  accessToken: string,
): Promise<boolean | null> {
  // Get all installations the user has access to
  const result = await fetchUserInstallations(accessToken);

  if (result.error && result.installations.length === 0) {
    // Complete failure - return unknown
    return null;
  }

  if (result.installations.length === 0) {
    // Successfully fetched, but no installations
    return false;
  }

  // Check each installation to see if it has access to the repo
  for (const installation of result.installations) {
    const hasAccess = await checkInstallationHasRepo(
      installation.id,
      repoFullName,
      accessToken
    );
    if (hasAccess === true) {
      return true;
    }
    // Continue checking other installations even if one fails
  }

  // If we had errors during fetch, we can't be sure the answer is "no"
  if (result.error) {
    return null;
  }

  return false;
}

// Check if a specific installation has access to a repo
// Returns: true (found), false (not found), null (error)
async function checkInstallationHasRepo(
  installationId: number,
  repoFullName: string,
  accessToken: string,
): Promise<boolean | null> {
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
    "User-Agent": "entire-api",
    "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
    Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
  };

  let page = 1;
  const perPage = 100;
  const maxPages = 10; // Cap at 1000 repos per installation

  while (page <= maxPages) {
    const url = `${GITHUB_API}/user/installations/${installationId}/repositories?per_page=${perPage}&page=${page}`;
    const response = await fetch(url, { headers });

    if (!response.ok) {
      // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
      response.body?.cancel();
      console.error(`checkInstallationHasRepo error for installation ${installationId}: ${response.status}`);
      return null;
    }

    const data = await response.json<{
      total_count: number;
      repositories: Array<{ full_name: string }>;
    }>();

    if (data.repositories.some((r) => r.full_name === repoFullName)) {
      return true;
    }

    if (data.repositories.length < perPage) {
      break;
    }
    page++;
  }

  return false;
}

// Cached version of checkRepoHasAppAccess - caches result in KV for 10 minutes
// Note: Cache is per-user since different users have different access to repos
export async function checkRepoHasAppAccessCached(
  repoFullName: string,
  userId: string,
  accessToken: string,
  cache: KVNamespace,
): Promise<boolean | null> {
  const cacheKey = `app_access:${userId}:${repoFullName}`;

  // Try cache first
  const cached = await cache.get(cacheKey);
  if (cached !== null) {
    if (cached === "true") return true;
    if (cached === "false") return false;
    return null; // "null" string
  }

  // Fetch fresh
  const result = await checkRepoHasAppAccess(repoFullName, accessToken);

  // Cache the result (10 min TTL - shorter since we can't easily invalidate per-user from webhooks)
  const cacheValue = result === null ? "null" : String(result);
  await cache.put(cacheKey, cacheValue, { expirationTtl: 60 * 10 });

  return result;
}

// Fetch user's contribution data
// Note: GitHub doesn't have a public API for contributions graph
// This uses the public profile page scraping approach or GraphQL
export async function fetchUserContributions(
  username: string,
  accessToken?: string,
): Promise<{
  total_count: number;
  contributions: Array<{ date: string; count: number }>;
}> {
  // If we have an access token, use GraphQL API
  if (accessToken) {
    const query = `
      query($username: String!) {
        user(login: $username) {
          contributionsCollection {
            contributionCalendar {
              totalContributions
              weeks {
                contributionDays {
                  date
                  contributionCount
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    `;

    const response = await fetch("https://api.github.com/graphql", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
        "User-Agent": "gh-social-api",
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({ query, variables: { username } }),
    });

    if (response.ok) {
      const data = await response.json<{
        data: {
          user: {
            contributionsCollection: {
              contributionCalendar: {
                totalContributions: number;
                weeks: Array<{
                  contributionDays: Array<{
                    date: string;
                    contributionCount: number;
                  }>;
                }>;
              };
            };
          };
        };
      }>();

      const calendar =
        data.data.user.contributionsCollection.contributionCalendar;

      const contributions = calendar.weeks.flatMap((week) =>
        week.contributionDays.map((day) => ({
          date: day.date,
          count: day.contributionCount,
        })),
      );

      return {
        total_count: calendar.totalContributions,
        contributions,
      };
    } else {
      // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
      response.body?.cancel();
    }
  }

  // Fallback: return empty data
  // In production, you might scrape the public profile or use a different approach
  return {
    total_count: 0,
    contributions: [],
  };
}

// Result from fetching commit activity
interface CommitActivityResult {
  weeks: number[];
  week_start: number;
}

// Fetch commit activity for a single repository
// Returns weekly commit totals for the last 52 weeks with week_start timestamp
async function fetchSingleRepoCommitActivity(
  repoFullName: string,
  accessToken?: string,
  retries = 3,
): Promise<CommitActivityResult | null> {
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
    "User-Agent": "entire-api",
    "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
  };

  if (accessToken) {
    headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${accessToken}`;
  }

  const response = await fetch(
    `${GITHUB_API}/repos/${repoFullName}/stats/commit_activity`,
    { headers },
  );

  // GitHub returns 202 if stats are being computed - retry after delay
  if (response.status === 202) {
    // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
    response.body?.cancel();
    if (retries > 0) {
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 2000));
      return fetchSingleRepoCommitActivity(
        repoFullName,
        accessToken,
        retries - 1,
      );
    }
    // Stats still computing after retries, return null
    return null;
  }

  // 204 No Content means no data available
  if (response.status === 204) {
    // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
    response.body?.cancel();
    return null;
  }

  if (!response.ok) {
    // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
    response.body?.cancel();
    // Return null for repos we can't access (404, 403, etc.)
    return null;
  }

  // Check if response has content before parsing
  const text = await response.text();
  if (!text || text.trim() === "") {
    return null;
  }

  let data: Array<{ days: number[]; total: number; week: number }>;
  try {
    data = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    // Invalid JSON response
    return null;
  }

  // GitHub returns empty array for repos with no commits
  if (!Array.isArray(data) || data.length === 0) {
    return null;
  }

  // Return array of weekly totals (52 weeks) with week_start timestamp
  // The first element's 'week' field is the Unix timestamp of week 0
  return {
    weeks: data.map((week) => week.total),
    week_start: data[0].week,
  };
}

  repos: Array<{ full_name: string }>,
  accessToken?: string,
): Promise<RepoCommitActivity[]> {
  // Fetch activity with limited concurrency to avoid stalling Workers
  const results = await mapWithConcurrency(
    repos,
    async (repo) => {
      try {
        const result = await fetchSingleRepoCommitActivity(
          repo.full_name,
          accessToken,
        );
        if (!result) return null;
        const activity: RepoCommitActivity = {
          repo_full_name: repo.full_name,
          weeks: result.weeks,
          week_start: result.week_start,
        };
        return activity;
      } catch (err) {
        // Log but don't fail the whole batch
        console.error(`Failed to fetch activity for ${repo.full_name}:`, err);
        return null;
      }
    },
    6,
  );

  // Filter out null results (failed fetches)
  return results.filter((r): r is RepoCommitActivity => r !== null);
}

// Fetch commits for a specific repository
export async function fetchRepoCommits(
  repoFullName: string,
  branch?: string,
  accessToken?: string,
  limit: number = 30,
  since?: string,
): Promise<CommitInfo[]> {
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
    "User-Agent": "entire-api",
    "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
  };

  if (accessToken) {
    headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${accessToken}`;
  }

  let url = `${GITHUB_API}/repos/${repoFullName}/commits?per_page=${limit}`;
  if (branch) {
    url += `&sha=${encodeURIComponent(branch)}`;
  }
  if (since) {
    url += `&since=${encodeURIComponent(since)}`;
  }

  const response = await fetch(url, { headers });

  if (!response.ok) {
    // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
    response.body?.cancel();
    throw new Error(`Failed to fetch commits: ${response.status}`);
  }

  const commits = await response.json<
    Array<{
      sha: string;
      commit: {
        message: string;
        author: {
          name: string;
          date: string;
        };
      };
      author: {
        login: string;
      } | null;
      html_url: string;
    }>
  >();

  return commits.map((c) => ({
    sha: c.sha,
    message: c.commit.message,
    author: c.commit.author.name,
    authorUsername: c.author?.login ?? "",
    date: c.commit.author.date,
    url: c.html_url,
  }));
}

// Fetch branches for a specific repository
export async function fetchRepoBranches(
  repoFullName: string,

): Promise<string[]> {
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",

  };

  if (accessToken) {

  }

// Parse git trailers from a commit message
// Trailers are key-value pairs at the end of a commit message in the format "Key: Value"
export function parseTrailers(message: string): Record<string, string> {
  const trailers: Record<string, string> = {};
  const lines = message.split("\n");

  // Trailers are at the end of the message, after a blank line
  // Work backwards to find them
  let inTrailers = false;
  for (let i = lines.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
    const line = lines[i].trim();

    // Empty line marks the boundary between body and trailers
    if (line === "") {
      if (inTrailers) break;
      continue;
    }

    // Check if line matches trailer format "Key: Value"
    const match = line.match(/^([A-Za-z0-9-]+):\s*(.+)$/);
    if (match) {
      inTrailers = true;
      trailers[match[1]] = match[2];
    } else if (inTrailers) {
      // Non-trailer line after we've seen trailers means we've gone too far
      break;
    }
  }

  return trailers;
}

// Fetch full details for a single commit (including files and patches)
export async function fetchCommitDetails(
  repoFullName: string,
  sha: string,
  accessToken?: string,
): Promise<CommitDetails> {
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
    "User-Agent": "entire-api",
    "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
  };

  if (accessToken) {
    headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${accessToken}`;
  }

  const response = await fetch(
    `${GITHUB_API}/repos/${repoFullName}/commits/${sha}`,
    { headers }
  );

  if (!response.ok) {
    // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
    response.body?.cancel();
    throw new Error(`Failed to fetch commit details: ${response.status}`);
  }

  const data = await response.json<{
    sha: string;
    commit: {
      message: string;
      author: {
        name: string;
        date: string;
      };
    };
    files?: Array<{
      filename: string;
      status: string;
      additions: number;
      deletions: number;
      patch?: string;
      previous_filename?: string;
    }>;
    stats?: {
      additions: number;
      deletions: number;

    };

  return {
    sha: data.sha,

    author: data.commit.author.name,

}

// Fetch file content at a specific commit
export async function fetchFileAtCommit(
  repoFullName: string,
  path: string,
  sha: string,
  accessToken?: string,
): Promise<string | null> {
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    Accept: "application/vnd.github.raw+json",
    "User-Agent": "entire-api",
    "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
  };

  if (accessToken) {
    headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${accessToken}`;
  }

  // Encode each path segment individually, not the whole path (/ must remain unencoded)
  const encodedPath = path.split("/").map(encodeURIComponent).join("/");
  const response = await fetch(
    `${GITHUB_API}/repos/${repoFullName}/contents/${encodedPath}?ref=${sha}`,
    { headers }
  );

  if (!response.ok) {
    // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
    response.body?.cancel();
    // File might not exist in this commit
    if (response.status === 404) {
      return null;
    }
    throw new Error(`Failed to fetch file: ${response.status}`);
  }

  // With Accept: application/vnd.github.raw+json, we get raw content directly
  return response.text();
}

// Fetch commits from both main and entire/sessions branches using REST API
export async function fetchBranchCommitsForCheckpoints(
  owner: string,
  repo: string,
  accessToken: string,
  mainBranch: string = "main",
  limit: number = 100,
  since?: string,
): Promise<{
  mainCommits: CommitInfo[];
  sessionCommits: CommitInfo[];
}> {
  const repoFullName = `${owner}/${repo}`;

  // Fetch both branches in parallel
  const [mainCommits, sessionCommits] = await Promise.all([
    fetchRepoCommits(repoFullName, mainBranch, accessToken, limit, since),
    fetchRepoCommits(repoFullName, "entire/sessions", accessToken, limit, since).catch(() => {
      // entire/sessions branch may not exist yet
      return [] as CommitInfo[];
    }),
  ]);

  return { mainCommits, sessionCommits };
}

// Extract checkpoint ID from a session commit message
// First line is "Checkpoint: <id>"
function extractSessionCheckpointId(message: string): string | null {
  const firstLine = message.split("\n")[0];
  const match = firstLine.match(/^Checkpoint:\s*([a-f0-9]+)$/i);
  return match ? match[1] : null;
}

// Build checkpoints by matching main branch commits (with Entire-Checkpoint trailer)
// to session branch commits (with Checkpoint: <id> first line)
export function buildCheckpoints(
  mainCommits: CommitInfo[],
  sessionCommits: CommitInfo[],
): PartialCheckpointInfo[] {
  // Build a map of session commits by their checkpoint ID
  const sessionByCheckpointId = new Map<string, CommitInfo>();
  for (const sessionCommit of sessionCommits) {
    const checkpointId = extractSessionCheckpointId(sessionCommit.message);
    if (checkpointId) {
      sessionByCheckpointId.set(checkpointId, sessionCommit);
    }
  }

  const checkpoints: PartialCheckpointInfo[] = [];

  // Go through main commits and find ones with Entire-Checkpoint trailer
  for (const commit of mainCommits) {
    const trailers = parseTrailers(commit.message);
    const checkpointId = trailers["Entire-Checkpoint"];

    if (!checkpointId) {
      continue;
    }

    // Find matching session commit
    const sessionCommit = sessionByCheckpointId.get(checkpointId);
    if (!sessionCommit) {
      continue;
    }

    checkpoints.push({
      commitSha: commit.sha,
      commitMessage: commit.message.split("\n")[0], // First line only
      commitAuthor: commit.author,
      commitAuthorUsername: commit.authorUsername,
      commitDate: commit.date,
      checkpointId, // e.g., "317248514d35" -> folder "31/7248514d35/"
    });
  }

  return checkpoints;
}

      throw new GitHubRateLimitError(
        "GitHub API rate limit exceeded",
        response.status,
        rateLimitCheck.resetAt
      );
    }

    if (!response.ok) {
      response.body?.cancel();
      // 404 means branch doesn't exist
      if (response.status === 404) {
        return results;
      }
      throw new Error(`Failed to fetch branch commits: ${response.status}`);
    }

    const commits = await response.json<
      Array<{
        sha: string;
        commit: {
          message: string;
          author: {
            name: string;
            date: string;
          };
        };
        author: {
          login: string;
        } | null;
        html_url: string;
      }>
    >();

    for (const commit of commits) {
      const trailers = parseTrailers(commit.commit.message);
      const checkpointId = trailers["Entire-Checkpoint"];

      if (checkpointId && targetCheckpointIds.has(checkpointId) && !results.has(checkpointId)) {
        results.set(checkpointId, {
          sha: commit.sha,
          message: commit.commit.message,
          author: commit.commit.author.name,
          authorUsername: commit.author?.login ?? "",
          date: commit.commit.author.date,
          url: commit.html_url,
        });
      }
    }

    totalFetched += commits.length;

    if (commits.length < perPage) {
      break;
    }
    page++;
  }

  return results;
}

const GITHUB_GRAPHQL = "https://api.github.com/graphql";

interface GraphQLResponse<T> {
  data?: T;

// Custom error class for rate limit detection
export class GitHubRateLimitError extends Error {
  constructor(
    message: string,
    public readonly status: number,
    public readonly resetAt?: number
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "GitHubRateLimitError";
  }
}

// Result type for GraphQL calls that may have partial data
export interface GraphQLResult<T> {
  data: T | null;
  errors: Array<{ message: string; path?: string[] }>;
  hasPartialData: boolean;
}

// Check if a response indicates rate limiting (429 or 403 with rate limit headers)
function isRateLimited(response: Response): { limited: boolean; resetAt?: number } {
  if (response.status === 429) {
    const resetHeader = response.headers.get("X-RateLimit-Reset");
    return { limited: true, resetAt: resetHeader ? parseInt(resetHeader, 10) : undefined };
  }

  if (response.status === 403) {
    const remaining = response.headers.get("X-RateLimit-Remaining");
    if (remaining === "0") {
      const resetHeader = response.headers.get("X-RateLimit-Reset");
      return { limited: true, resetAt: resetHeader ? parseInt(resetHeader, 10) : undefined };
    }
  }

  return { limited: false };
}

// GraphQL call that throws on errors (original behavior for backwards compatibility)
export async function githubGraphQL<T>(
  token: string,
  query: string,
  variables: Record<string, unknown> = {}
): Promise<T> {
  const response = await fetch(GITHUB_GRAPHQL, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
      "User-Agent": "entire-api",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ query, variables }),
  });

  // Check for rate limiting (429 or 403 with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0)
  const rateLimitCheck = isRateLimited(response);
  if (rateLimitCheck.limited) {
    // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
    response.body?.cancel();
    throw new GitHubRateLimitError(
      "GitHub API rate limit exceeded",
      response.status,
      rateLimitCheck.resetAt
    );
  }

  if (!response.ok) {
    // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
    response.body?.cancel();
    throw new Error(`GitHub GraphQL error: ${response.status}`);
  }

  const result = await response.json<GraphQLResponse<T>>();

  if (result.errors && result.errors.length > 0) {
    const errorMessages = result.errors.map((e) => e.message).join(", ");
    throw new Error(`GitHub GraphQL errors: ${errorMessages}`);
  }

  if (!result.data) {
    throw new Error("GitHub GraphQL returned no data");
  }

  return result.data;
}

// GraphQL call that returns partial data when available (for batch operations)
// Returns data even if some errors occurred, allowing partial success handling
export async function githubGraphQLPartial<T>(
  token: string,
  query: string,
  variables: Record<string, unknown> = {}
): Promise<GraphQLResult<T>> {
  const response = await fetch(GITHUB_GRAPHQL, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
      "User-Agent": "entire-api",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ query, variables }),
  });

  // Check for rate limiting (429 or 403 with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0)
  const rateLimitCheck = isRateLimited(response);
  if (rateLimitCheck.limited) {
    // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
    response.body?.cancel();
    throw new GitHubRateLimitError(
      "GitHub API rate limit exceeded",
      response.status,
      rateLimitCheck.resetAt
    );
  }

  if (!response.ok) {
    // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
    response.body?.cancel();
    throw new Error(`GitHub GraphQL error: ${response.status}`);
  }

  const result = await response.json<GraphQLResponse<T>>();

  return {
    data: result.data ?? null,
    errors: result.errors ?? [],
    hasPartialData: result.data !== undefined && result.errors !== undefined && result.errors.length > 0,
  };
}

// Batch result type for tracking partial failures
export interface BatchResult<T> {
  data: Map<string, T>;
  failedItems: string[];
  errors: string[];
}

// Batch fetch commit stats using GraphQL
// Returns a map of SHA -> { additions, deletions, filesChanged } along with any failures
export async function fetchCommitStatsBatch(
  repoFullName: string,
  shas: string[],
  token: string
): Promise<BatchResult<{ additions: number; deletions: number; filesChanged: number }>> {
  const results: BatchResult<{ additions: number; deletions: number; filesChanged: number }> = {
    data: new Map(),
    failedItems: [],
    errors: [],
  };

  // Filter to valid SHAs to prevent GraphQL injection
  const invalidShas: string[] = [];
  const validShas = shas.filter((sha) => {
    if (!isValidSha(sha)) {
      console.warn(`[github-graphql] Skipping invalid SHA: ${sha.slice(0, 10)}...`);
      invalidShas.push(sha);
      return false;
    }
    return true;
  });

  // Track invalid SHAs as failed items
  results.failedItems.push(...invalidShas);

  if (validShas.length === 0) return results;

  const [owner, repo] = repoFullName.split("/");

  // Chunk into batches of 50 to avoid query size limits
  const BATCH_SIZE = 50;
  for (let i = 0; i < validShas.length; i += BATCH_SIZE) {
    const batch = validShas.slice(i, i + BATCH_SIZE);

    // Build dynamic query with aliases for each commit
    const commitQueries = batch
      .map((sha, idx) => `c${idx}: object(oid: "${sha}") { ... on Commit { additions deletions changedFilesIfAvailable } }`)
      .join("\n");

    const query = `
      query CommitStats($owner: String!, $repo: String!) {
        repository(owner: $owner, name: $repo) {
          ${commitQueries}
        }
      }
    `;

    try {
      // Use partial data handling to extract successful results even if some fail
      const result = await githubGraphQLPartial<{
        repository: Record<string, { additions: number; deletions: number; changedFilesIfAvailable: number | null } | null>;
      }>(token, query, { owner, repo });

      if (result.hasPartialData) {
        console.warn(`[github-graphql] Partial success in commit stats batch:`, result.errors.map(e => e.message).join(", "));
      }

      if (result.data?.repository) {
        batch.forEach((sha, idx) => {
          const commit = result.data!.repository[`c${idx}`];
          if (commit) {
            results.data.set(sha, {
              additions: commit.additions,
              deletions: commit.deletions,
              filesChanged: commit.changedFilesIfAvailable ?? 0,
            });
          } else {
            // This specific commit failed - track it
            results.failedItems.push(sha);
          }
        });
      } else if (result.errors.length > 0) {
        // No data at all - whole batch failed
        const errorMsg = result.errors.map(e => e.message).join(", ");
        console.error(`[github-graphql] Failed to fetch commit stats batch:`, errorMsg);
        results.failedItems.push(...batch);
        results.errors.push(`Batch ${i / BATCH_SIZE + 1}: ${errorMsg}`);
      }
    } catch (err) {
      const errorMsg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
      console.error(`[github-graphql] Failed to fetch commit stats batch:`, errorMsg);
      results.failedItems.push(...batch);
      results.errors.push(`Batch ${i / BATCH_SIZE + 1}: ${errorMsg}`);
    }
  }

  return results;
}

export async function fetchSessionDataBatch(
  repoFullName: string,
  checkpointIds: string[],
  token: string
): Promise<BatchResult<SessionData>> {
  const results: BatchResult<SessionData> = {
    data: new Map(),
    failedItems: [],
    errors: [],
  };

  // Filter to valid checkpoint IDs to prevent GraphQL injection
  const invalidIds: string[] = [];
  const validCheckpointIds = checkpointIds.filter((id) => {
    if (!isValidCheckpointId(id)) {
      console.warn(`[github-graphql] Skipping invalid checkpoint ID: ${id.slice(0, 10)}...`);
      invalidIds.push(id);
      return false;
    }
    return true;
  });

  // Track invalid IDs as failed items
  results.failedItems.push(...invalidIds);

  if (validCheckpointIds.length === 0) return results;

  const [owner, repo] = repoFullName.split("/");

  // Chunk into batches of 20 (40 blobs per batch - metadata + prompt)
  const BATCH_SIZE = 20;
  for (let i = 0; i < validCheckpointIds.length; i += BATCH_SIZE) {
    const batch = validCheckpointIds.slice(i, i + BATCH_SIZE);

    // Build dynamic query with aliases for each checkpoint's files
    const fileQueries = batch
      .map((checkpointId, idx) => {
        const folderPath = `${checkpointId.slice(0, 2)}/${checkpointId.slice(2)}`;
        return `
          m${idx}: object(expression: "entire/sessions:${folderPath}/metadata.json") { ... on Blob { text } }
          p${idx}: object(expression: "entire/sessions:${folderPath}/prompt.txt") { ... on Blob { text } }
        `;
      })
      .join("\n");

    const query = `
      query SessionData($owner: String!, $repo: String!) {
        repository(owner: $owner, name: $repo) {
          ${fileQueries}
        }
      }
    `;

    try {
      // Use partial data handling to extract successful results even if some fail
      const result = await githubGraphQLPartial<{
        repository: Record<string, { text: string } | null>;
      }>(token, query, { owner, repo });

      if (result.hasPartialData) {
        console.warn(`[github-graphql] Partial success in session data batch:`, result.errors.map(e => e.message).join(", "));
      }

      if (result.data?.repository) {
        batch.forEach((checkpointId, idx) => {
          const metadata = result.data!.repository[`m${idx}`];
          const prompt = result.data!.repository[`p${idx}`];

          // If both metadata and prompt are null, this checkpoint may not exist
          // Still record it with defaults so we don't repeatedly try to fetch it
          let sessionData: SessionData = {
            prompt: prompt?.text?.split("\n")[0] ?? null,
            agent: "Claude Code",
            steps: 1,
            sessionCount: 1,
            strategy: null,
            createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
            branch: null,
            sessionId: null,
            filesTouched: null,
            sessionIds: null,
            transcriptUuidAtStart: null,
            transcriptLinesAtStart: null,
            inputTokens: null,
            cacheCreationTokens: null,
            cacheReadTokens: null,
            outputTokens: null,
            apiCallCount: null,
          };

          if (metadata?.text) {
            try {
              const parsed = JSON.parse(metadata.text);
              const tokenUsage = parsed.token_usage ?? {};
              sessionData = {
                ...sessionData,
                agent: parsed.agent ?? "Claude Code",
                steps: parsed.steps_count ?? parsed.checkpoints_count ?? 1,
                sessionCount: parsed.session_count ?? 1,
                strategy: parsed.strategy ?? null,
                createdAt: parsed.created_at ?? new Date().toISOString(),
                branch: parsed.branch ?? null,
                sessionId: parsed.session_id ?? null,
                filesTouched: Array.isArray(parsed.files_touched) ? parsed.files_touched : null,
                sessionIds: Array.isArray(parsed.session_ids) ? parsed.session_ids : null,
                transcriptUuidAtStart: parsed.transcript_uuid_at_start ?? null,
                transcriptLinesAtStart: typeof parsed.transcript_lines_at_start === "number" ? parsed.transcript_lines_at_start : null,
                inputTokens: typeof tokenUsage.input_tokens === "number" ? tokenUsage.input_tokens : null,
                cacheCreationTokens: typeof tokenUsage.cache_creation_tokens === "number" ? tokenUsage.cache_creation_tokens : null,
                cacheReadTokens: typeof tokenUsage.cache_read_tokens === "number" ? tokenUsage.cache_read_tokens : null,
                outputTokens: typeof tokenUsage.output_tokens === "number" ? tokenUsage.output_tokens : null,
                apiCallCount: typeof tokenUsage.api_call_count === "number" ? tokenUsage.api_call_count : null,
              };
            } catch {
              // Invalid JSON, use defaults
            }
          }

          results.data.set(checkpointId, sessionData);
        });
      } else if (result.errors.length > 0) {
        // No data at all - whole batch failed
        const errorMsg = result.errors.map(e => e.message).join(", ");
        console.error(`[github-graphql] Failed to fetch session data batch:`, errorMsg);
        results.failedItems.push(...batch);
        results.errors.push(`Batch ${i / BATCH_SIZE + 1}: ${errorMsg}`);
      }
    } catch (err) {
      const errorMsg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
      console.error(`[github-graphql] Failed to fetch session data batch:`, errorMsg);
      results.failedItems.push(...batch);
      results.errors.push(`Batch ${i / BATCH_SIZE + 1}: ${errorMsg}`);
    }
  }

  return results;
}

// Fetch user's repositories with all data (for syncing to DB)
// Paginates through all pages (max 10 pages = 1000 repos to avoid runaway requests)
export async function fetchUserReposWithForks(
  username: string,
  accessToken?: string,
): Promise<GitHubRepoRaw[]> {
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
    "User-Agent": "gh-social-api",
    "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",

  }

      : `${GITHUB_API}/users/${username}/repos?sort=updated&per_page=${perPage}&page=${page}`;

// Check if a branch exists in a repository
// Returns: true (exists), false (doesn't exist), null (error/unknown)
export async function checkBranchExists(
  repoFullName: string,
  branchName: string,
  accessToken: string,
): Promise<boolean | null> {
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
    "User-Agent": "entire-api",
    "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
    Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
  };

  const url = `${GITHUB_API}/repos/${repoFullName}/branches/${encodeURIComponent(branchName)}`;
  const response = await fetch(url, { headers });

  if (response.ok) {
    // GitHub may redirect branch names (e.g., master -> main for default branch)
    // Verify the returned branch name actually matches what we requested
    const data = await response.json() as { name?: string };
    if (data.name !== branchName) {
      console.log(`[checkBranchExists] ${repoFullName}/${branchName} -> redirected to ${data.name}, treating as not found`);
      return false;
    }
    return true;
  }

  // Cancel body for non-OK responses
  response.body?.cancel();

  // 404 = branch doesn't exist (definitive answer)
  if (response.status === 404) {
    return false;
  }

  // 403/429/5xx = unknown (rate limit, auth issue, server error)
  console.error(`checkBranchExists error for ${repoFullName}/${branchName}: ${response.status}`);
  return null;
}

  // If we had errors during fetch, we can't be sure the answer is "no"
  if (result.error) {
    return null;
  }

  return false;
}

// Check if a specific installation has access to a repo
// Returns: true (found), false (not found), null (error)
async function checkInstallationHasRepo(
  installationId: number,
  repoFullName: string,
  accessToken: string,
): Promise<boolean | null> {
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
    "User-Agent": "entire-api",
    "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
    Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
  };

  let page = 1;
  const perPage = 100;
  const maxPages = 10; // Cap at 1000 repos per installation

  while (page <= maxPages) {
    const url = `${GITHUB_API}/user/installations/${installationId}/repositories?per_page=${perPage}&page=${page}`;
    const response = await fetch(url, { headers });

    if (!response.ok) {
      // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
      response.body?.cancel();
      console.error(`checkInstallationHasRepo error for installation ${installationId}: ${response.status}`);
      return null;
    }

    const data = await response.json<{
      total_count: number;
      repositories: Array<{ full_name: string }>;
    }>();

    if (data.repositories.some((r) => r.full_name === repoFullName)) {
      return true;
    }

    if (data.repositories.length < perPage) {
      break;
    }
    page++;
  }

  return false;
}

// Cached version of checkRepoHasAppAccess - caches result in KV for 10 minutes
// Note: Cache is per-user since different users have different access to repos
export async function checkRepoHasAppAccessCached(
  repoFullName: string,
  userId: string,
  accessToken: string,
  cache: KVNamespace,
): Promise<boolean | null> {
  const cacheKey = `app_access:${userId}:${repoFullName}`;

  // Try cache first
  const cached = await cache.get(cacheKey);
  if (cached !== null) {
    if (cached === "true") return true;
    if (cached === "false") return false;
    return null; // "null" string
  }

  // Fetch fresh
  const result = await checkRepoHasAppAccess(repoFullName, accessToken);

  // Cache the result (10 min TTL - shorter since we can't easily invalidate per-user from webhooks)
  const cacheValue = result === null ? "null" : String(result);
  await cache.put(cacheKey, cacheValue, { expirationTtl: 60 * 10 });

  return result;
}

// Fetch user's contribution data
// Note: GitHub doesn't have a public API for contributions graph
// This uses the public profile page scraping approach or GraphQL
export async function fetchUserContributions(
  username: string,
  accessToken?: string,
): Promise<{
  total_count: number;
  contributions: Array<{ date: string; count: number }>;
}> {
  // If we have an access token, use GraphQL API
  if (accessToken) {
    const query = `
      query($username: String!) {
        user(login: $username) {
          contributionsCollection {
            contributionCalendar {
              totalContributions
              weeks {
                contributionDays {
                  date
                  contributionCount
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    `;

    const response = await fetch("https://api.github.com/graphql", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
        "User-Agent": "gh-social-api",
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({ query, variables: { username } }),
    });

    if (response.ok) {
      const data = await response.json<{
        data: {
          user: {
            contributionsCollection: {
              contributionCalendar: {
                totalContributions: number;
                weeks: Array<{
                  contributionDays: Array<{
                    date: string;
                    contributionCount: number;
                  }>;
                }>;
              };
            };
          };
        };
      }>();

      const calendar =
        data.data.user.contributionsCollection.contributionCalendar;

      const contributions = calendar.weeks.flatMap((week) =>
        week.contributionDays.map((day) => ({
          date: day.date,
          count: day.contributionCount,
        })),
      );

      return {
        total_count: calendar.totalContributions,
        contributions,
      };
    } else {
      // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
      response.body?.cancel();
    }
  }

  // Fallback: return empty data
  // In production, you might scrape the public profile or use a different approach
  return {
    total_count: 0,
    contributions: [],
  };
}

// Result from fetching commit activity
interface CommitActivityResult {
  weeks: number[];
  week_start: number;
}

// Fetch commit activity for a single repository
// Returns weekly commit totals for the last 52 weeks with week_start timestamp
async function fetchSingleRepoCommitActivity(
  repoFullName: string,
  accessToken?: string,
  retries = 3,
): Promise<CommitActivityResult | null> {
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
    "User-Agent": "entire-api",
    "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
  };

  if (accessToken) {
    headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${accessToken}`;
  }

  const response = await fetch(
    `${GITHUB_API}/repos/${repoFullName}/stats/commit_activity`,
    { headers },
  );

  // GitHub returns 202 if stats are being computed - retry after delay
  if (response.status === 202) {
    // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
    response.body?.cancel();
    if (retries > 0) {
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 2000));
      return fetchSingleRepoCommitActivity(
        repoFullName,
        accessToken,
        retries - 1,
      );
    }
    // Stats still computing after retries, return null
    return null;
  }

  // 204 No Content means no data available
  if (response.status === 204) {
    // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
    response.body?.cancel();
    return null;
  }

  if (!response.ok) {
    // Cancel the response body to avoid stalled connections in Workers
    response.body?.cancel();
    // Return null for repos we can't access (404, 403, etc.)
    return null;
  }

  // Check if response has content before parsing
  const text = await response.text();
  if (!text || text.trim() === "") {
    return null;
  }

  let data: Array<{ days: number[]; total: number; week: number }>;
  try {
    data = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    // Invalid JSON response
    return null;
  }

  // GitHub returns empty array for repos with no commits
  if (!Array.isArray(data) || data.length === 0) {
    return null;
  }

  // Return array of weekly totals (52 weeks) with week_start timestamp
  // The first element's 'week' field is the Unix timestamp of week 0
  return {
    weeks: data.map((week) => week.total),
    week_start: data[0].week,
  };
}

// Parse git trailers from a commit message
// Trailers are key-value pairs at the end of a commit message in the format "Key: Value"
export function parseTrailers(message: string): Record<string, string> {
  const trailers: Record<string, string> = {};
  const lines = message.split("\n");

  // Trailers are at the end of the message, after a blank line
  // Work backwards to find them
  let inTrailers = false;
  for (let i = lines.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
    const line = lines[i].trim();

    // Empty line marks the boundary between body and trailers
    if (line === "") {
      if (inTrailers) break;
      continue;
    }

    // Check if line matches trailer format "Key: Value"
    const match = line.match(/^([A-Za-z0-9-]+):\s*(.+)$/);
    if (match) {
      inTrailers = true;
      trailers[match[1]] = match[2];
    } else if (inTrailers) {
      // Non-trailer line after we've seen trailers means we've gone too far
      break;
    }
  }

  return trailers;
}

  return response.text();
}

export async function fetchBranchCommitsForCheckpoints(
  owner: string,
  repo: string,
  accessToken: string,
  mainBranch: string = "main",
  limit: number = 100,
  since?: string,
): Promise<{
  mainCommits: CommitInfo[];
  sessionCommits: CommitInfo[];
}> {
  const repoFullName = `${owner}/${repo}`;

  // Fetch both branches in parallel
  const [mainCommits, sessionCommits] = await Promise.all([
    fetchRepoCommits(repoFullName, mainBranch, accessToken, limit, since),
    fetchRepoCommits(repoFullName, "entire/sessions", accessToken, limit, since).catch(() => {
      // entire/sessions branch may not exist yet
      return [] as CommitInfo[];
    }),
  ]);

  return { mainCommits, sessionCommits };
}

// Extract checkpoint ID from a session commit message
// First line is "Checkpoint: <id>"
function extractSessionCheckpointId(message: string): string | null {
  const firstLine = message.split("\n")[0];
  const match = firstLine.match(/^Checkpoint:\s*([a-f0-9]+)$/i);
  return match ? match[1] : null;
}

// Build checkpoints by matching main branch commits (with Entire-Checkpoint trailer)
// to session branch commits (with Checkpoint: <id> first line)
export function buildCheckpoints(
  mainCommits: CommitInfo[],
  sessionCommits: CommitInfo[],
): PartialCheckpointInfo[] {
  // Build a map of session commits by their checkpoint ID
  const sessionByCheckpointId = new Map<string, CommitInfo>();
  for (const sessionCommit of sessionCommits) {
    const checkpointId = extractSessionCheckpointId(sessionCommit.message);
    if (checkpointId) {
      sessionByCheckpointId.set(checkpointId, sessionCommit);
    }
  }

  const checkpoints: PartialCheckpointInfo[] = [];

  // Go through main commits and find ones with Entire-Checkpoint trailer
  for (const commit of mainCommits) {
    const trailers = parseTrailers(commit.message);
    const checkpointId = trailers["Entire-Checkpoint"];

    if (!checkpointId) {
      continue;
    }

    // Find matching session commit
    const sessionCommit = sessionByCheckpointId.get(checkpointId);
    if (!sessionCommit) {
      continue;
    }

    checkpoints.push({
      commitSha: commit.sha,
      commitMessage: commit.message.split("\n")[0], // First line only
      commitAuthor: commit.author,
      commitAuthorUsername: commit.authorUsername,
      commitDate: commit.date,
      checkpointId, // e.g., "317248514d35" -> folder "31/7248514d35/"
    });
  }

  return checkpoints;
}
